Get speech turns: consecutive actions by one speaker, merged

Source: R/query-views.R
get_speech_turns.Rd

Reads the v_speech_turns_context view: one row per turn, where a turn is the run of consecutive actions in a sitting that share a turn_no (actions with a missing or zero turn_no, and non-speech actions, belong to no turn). The view carries the sitting's date, chamber and parliament, the turn's first action's name_raw, and the party at the time.

Usage

get_speech_turns(
  member = NULL,
  party = NULL,
  parliament_id = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  sitting_id = NULL,
  resolution = NULL,
  include_text = TRUE,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

member

Character vector of member PHIDs, matched against the turn's PHID. A PHID that matches no member is an error; look one up with find_member().

party

Party ids (numbers) or party names or abbreviations (strings), matched against the party at the time; see get_speeches().

parliament_id

Filter on the sitting's parliament_id: a vector of values or in_range().

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

from, to

Sitting-date bounds, inclusive: a year (covering the whole year), a Date, or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string. NULL leaves that end open.

sitting_id

Filter on sitting_id: a vector of values or matches_pattern().

resolution

Filter on the turn's resolution: a character vector of values such as "resolved" or "sentinel", or matches_pattern(). NA is not accepted; see Details.

include_text

If TRUE (the default), add the content column. Results with content are held to the lower size ceiling, getOption("ausparl.max_rows_text").

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per turn, ordered by sitting_id then turn_no, with columns sitting_id, date, chamber, parliament_id, turn_no, first_action_id, n_actions, PHID, name_raw, resolution, party_id_at_time, party_at_time, has_quote, is_quote, and content when include_text = TRUE. Zero rows if nothing matches. With collect = FALSE, an unordered lazy table with the same columns.

Details

Turns, not actions. get_speeches() and get_actions() return one row per action: a speech broken by interjections or continued across pages is several rows there. Here it is one row, n_actions says how many actions it merges, and content is their text joined with a blank line ("\n\n"), in document order. The turn is identified by sitting_id and turn_no; first_action_id is the id of its first action, for joining back to action-level tables. No turn-type filter is applied: every turn in the view is returned, whatever its actions' types.

Quoted passages. Two columns describe quotations, computed over the turn's actions:

  • has_quote is TRUE when any action in the turn is flagged as containing quoted material (actions.has_quote). It is coarse: the turn quotes something somewhere.

  • is_quote is TRUE when every action in the turn is a quote (action_type = "quote"): the whole turn is a passage read into the record, not the speaker's own words.

Turns that are read-out passages are kept; drop them with dplyr::filter(!is_quote).

Speaker. PHID, name_raw and resolution are those of the turn's first action. Turns by the presiding officer (resolution = "sentinel"), and turns whose speaker is not one matched member ("collective", "unknown", "unmatched", "ambiguous", "non_member", or a missing resolution), are all kept, with PHID NA where there is no member. A member filter keeps only the turns of those members. resolution filters on the stored values and cannot select a missing (NA) resolution: such turns are returned only when resolution = NULL; to keep only them, use collect = FALSE and dplyr::filter(is.na(resolution)).

Party. party_at_time is the party of the turn's first action's speaker on the sitting date, not the member's current party, and party_id_at_time its party_id. party is resolved as in get_speeches().

Order and laziness. A collected result is ordered by sitting_id and then turn_no, and limit keeps the first rows in that order. With collect = FALSE the result is an unordered lazy table that works as a parameterised view: filter, join and aggregate it in DuckDB (for example with dplyr::count()) before collecting. Stored values are returned unchanged.

See also

get_speeches(), get_sitting_timeline(), find_member()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
get_speech_turns(party = "ALP", from = 2002, to = 2002, include_text = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 78 × 14
#>    sitting_id date       chamber parliament_id turn_no first_action_id n_actions
#>    <chr>      <date>     <chr>           <int>   <int> <chr>               <dbl>
#>  1 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40       2 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  2 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40       6 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  3 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      10 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  4 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      15 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  5 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      19 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  6 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      25 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  7 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      27 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  8 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      29 house_2002-10-…         1
#>  9 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      31 house_2002-10-…         1
#> 10 house_200… 2002-10-15 house              40      39 house_2002-10-…         1
#> # ℹ 68 more rows
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: PHID <chr>, name_raw <chr>, resolution <chr>,
#> #   party_id_at_time <int>, party_at_time <chr>, has_quote <lgl>,
#> #   is_quote <lgl>
howard <- find_member("john howard")$PHID
get_speech_turns(member = howard, columns = c("date", "n_actions", "is_quote"))
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   date       n_actions is_quote
#>   <date>         <dbl> <lgl>   
#> 1 1990-09-17         1 FALSE   
#> 2 1990-09-17         1 FALSE   
#> 3 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
#> 4 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
#> 5 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
#> 6 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
#> 7 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
#> 8 2002-10-15         1 FALSE   
db_disconnect()
